caption:
The Old Fashioned, explained 🥃 The original 1806 cocktail, still a bar classic.

In 1806 a New York newspaper defined a “cocktail” as spirit, sugar, water and bitters. As fancier drinks arrived, people asked for it the “old-fashioned” way, and by 1880 the name was in print.

The IBA recipe: 45 ml bourbon or rye whiskey, 1 sugar cube, a few dashes of aromatic bitters, a few dashes of plain water. Soak the sugar with the bitters and water, muddle, add ice and the whiskey, stir gently. Garnish with orange and a cocktail cherry.

Save this for your next home bar night 🔖 and tag the friend who makes the best Old Fashioned.

Drink slow. Never drink and drive. 18+
